pre_mortem: It is Monday and both Chicago rush unders lost. Minnesota's 3.14 YPC was one game against a team that would not run, and Chicago's line, with nobody on the injury report, opened the same lanes as week 1. Swift got the favorite's late carries, broke a 40-yard run, and cleared 124.5, and Monangai mixed in a dozen carries and ripped another long one because the 80 percent blitz left the second level light, the same look that allowed 7 passes of 20-plus. Or the game became a blowout and both backs piled garbage carries at a high rate. There is no play-by-play, so week 1 may have been power running rather than a fluke, and these rungs are stand-in medians, not a market that has already shaded the opponent. Unsaved wind would only add rush attempts and make the unders worse. That counter is real, which is why Swift stays a lean and the strong Monangai leg is flagged rather than sized.
